name: Calchaqui
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog refs are only wordlists/toponymy/ethnohistory (Nardi 1979, Serrano 1936); no phonological description of Kakan/Calchaqui exists

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain 2005 [rev. 2013]. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: entry CALCHAQUÍ / KAKÁN. 4 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; states the language is totally unknown apart from toponymy and onomastics ('se desconoce totalmente el idioma, que se conoce fragmentariamente a través de la toponimia'); bibliography lists no phonological description.

sources.citation: Carvajal Lazo, Herman 1990. Algunas referencias sobre la lengua de los diaguitas chilenos, II parte. Logos (Universidad de La Serena) 2: 1-15.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; states (p. ~12, scanned) that the small, mostly onomastic lexical inventory 'no permite en absoluto la reconstrucción morfosintáctica e incluso fonológica de esta lengua' and that no colonial grammar survives (Barzana's is lost).

sources.citation: Carvajal Lazo, Herman 1989. Algunas referencias sobre la lengua de los diaguitas chilenos, I parte. Logos (La Serena) 1: 1-11.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: First part of the Carvajal survey (part II downloaded); unlikely to add prosodic information but completes the record.

sources.citation: Nardi, Ricardo L. J. 1979. El kakán, lengua de los Diaguitas. Sapiens 3: 1-33. Chivilcoy: Museo Arqueológico Dr. Osvaldo F. A. Menghin. (educarchile.cl re-typeset transcription, 34 pp., via the Internet Archive)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 7 'Consideraciones fonéticas y fonológicas' treats only consonant series inferable from colonial spellings of toponyms/anthroponyms and states no phonetic or phonemic reconstruction is attempted; nothing on word accent of Kakán. Only accent-related remark is in sec. 5: 'es posible que haya quedado algún substrato kakán en la entonación del Noroeste sobre todo en la extraña curva melódica y la acentuación en primera sílaba de algunas palabras dentro del grupo fónico que ocurre, por ejemplo, en ciertas regiones riojanas' -- a speculation about regional Spanish, not a statement about Kakán…
Nothing on stress; only quotes Lozano's 'gutural' characterisation and lists palatal consonants after Nardi.

sources.citation: Martín, Eusebia Herminia 1964. Notas sobre el cacán y la toponimia del NOA argentino. Cuadernos de Lingüística Indígena 2. Buenos Aires: UBA.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The other dedicated linguistic treatment of Cacán toponymy; could conceivably comment on accentuation of surviving toponyms, though it cannot describe Kakán stress proper.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F. H. & Pieter C. Muysken 2004. The Languages of the Andes (section on Diaguita/Kakán). Cambridge: CUP.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: Authoritative modern survey; would confirm that nothing is known of Kakán phonology beyond spellings of names.

sources.citation: Barzana (Bárcena), Alonso de, ca. 1590. Arte y vocabulario de la lengua kakana / 'Lexica et praecepta grammatica' (manuscript, lost).
